parse.title: Increased heart rate
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>[[File:Tachycardia ECG paper.svg|250px|thumb|right| Heartrate above 100BPM]] '''Increased heart rate'''  or '''tachycardia''' is described as a heart rate that is faster than the normal heart rate at rest. The average healthy human heart normally beats 60 to 100 times a minute when a person is at rest. When the heart rate fluctuates to higher levels over 100 BPM, it is described as tachycardia or an abnormally high heart rate. 

It is worth noting that increased heart rate can often be a result of psychological symptoms as a natural adrenal response to [[anxiety]], [[paranoia]], shock, and fear. 

Increased heart rate is most commonly induced under the influence of [[dosage#heavy|heavy]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[stimulation|stimulating]] compounds, such as traditional [[stimulant|stimulants]], certain [[psychedelic|psychedelics]], and certain [[dissociative|dissociatives]]. This is thought to occur as a direct result of [[Dopamine|dopaminergic]] or [[Adrenaline#The_Adrenergic_System|adrenergic]] modulation.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Billman, G. E.)) | journal=The FASEB Journal | title=Mechanisms responsible for the cardiotoxic effects of cocaine | volume=4 | issue=8 | pages=2469–2475 | date= May 1990 | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1096/fasebj.4.8.2185973 | issn=0892-6638 | doi=10.1096/fasebj.4.8.2185973}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ferreira, M. T.)), ((Ferreira, R.)), ((Carvalho, F.)), ((Duarte, J. A.)) | journal=Revista portuguesa de cardiologia | title=Effect of physical exercise on markers of acute cardiotoxicity induced by d-amphetamine in an animal model | volume=25 | issue=11 | pages=983–996 | date=1 November 2006 | issn=2174-2030}}</ref> However, it can also occur under the influence of [[deliriant|deliriants]] due to the way in which they inhibit [[acetylcholine]], one of the main modulaters of heart rate in the peripheral nervous system.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Triposkiadis, F.)), ((Karayannis, G.)), ((Giamouzis, G.)), ((Skoularigis, J.)), ((Louridas, G.)), ((Butler, J.)) | journal=Journal of the American College of Cardiology | title=The Sympathetic Nervous System in Heart Failure | volume=54 | issue=19 | pages=1747–1762 | date= November 2009 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0735109709016891 | issn=07351097 | doi=10.1016/j.jacc.2009.05.015}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Akselrod, S.)), ((Gordon, D.)), ((Ubel, F. A.)), ((Shannon, D. C.)), ((Berger, A. C.)), ((Cohen, R. J.)) | journal=Science | title=Power Spectrum Analysis of Heart Rate Fluctuation: A Quantitative Probe of Beat-to-Beat Cardiovascular Control | volume=213 | issue=4504 | pages=220–222 | date=10 July 1981 | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.6166045 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.6166045}}</ref>
